_about: Everything on retcalc.app that goes stale with time. One entry per thing to update. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. last_updated: when the figures were last changed or checked against the source and found current. next_due: when to look again. Edit this file when an update is done, then run python3 upkeep/check.py --write. See upkeep/UPKEEP.md.

items.name: Federal income tax brackets and deductions
items.what: Federal brackets, standard deduction, long-term capital gains breakpoints, the age-65 extra standard deduction, and the 2025-2028 senior deduction.
where: web/lib/engine/math.js: FED_2026, FED_STD, LTCG_2026, SENIOR_ADDL, SENIOR_BONUS
items.source: IRS revenue procedure for the coming tax year (Rev. Proc. 2025-32 gave 2026), usually out in late October
items.cadence: Yearly. Prepare in November or December; switch on January 1
items.notes: Statutory figures that are not indexed (NIIT, Social Security provisional-income thresholds) only change with a new law. The senior deduction ends after tax year 2028.

items.name: Social Security wage base and benefit bend points
items.what: The Social Security tax wage cap (also the cap on earnings the benefit estimate counts) and the two bend points in the benefit formula.
items.source: SSA's annual COLA and wage-base fact sheet, released in October
items.cadence: Yearly. Switch with the federal tax figures on January 1
items.notes: FICA.ssCap and SS_CAP must stay the same number.

items.name: State income tax brackets and deductions (50 states and DC)
items.what: Every state's brackets, standard deduction, personal exemption and credits. Illinois has extra detail (exemption cliff, 65+ amount).
items.source: Tax Foundation, State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets (as of January 1), usually published in February; state revenue departments for detail
items.cadence: Yearly, after the Tax Foundation survey comes out
items.notes: States sometimes change rates mid-year; the law-watch item covers that.

items.name: State rules for retirement income
items.what: Which states tax Social Security, pension and IRA exclusions, extra deductions or credits at 65, and states with no early-withdrawal penalty add-on.
where: web/lib/engine/plan.js: PL_NOEXP (also used by the Bridge)
items.source: State revenue departments; Tax Foundation and AARP state guides as a cross-check
items.cadence: Yearly, early in the year
items.notes: Several entries quote dollar amounts in their notes (Maryland's pension exclusion, Minnesota's AGI limits); those change yearly too.

items.name: Medicare Part B premium and IRMAA tiers
items.what: The standard Part B premium and the income tiers that raise Part B and Part D for higher earners.
where: web/lib/engine/math.js: IRMAA (the Healthcare tool reads it through HC_IRMAA)
items.source: CMS Medicare Parts A and B premiums and deductibles fact sheet, usually out in October or November
items.cadence: Yearly. Switch on January 1

items.name: Medicare Part D and Medigap cost estimates
items.what: The average standalone Part D premium and the rough monthly range for a Medigap Plan G policy at 65.
items.source: CMS Part D premium announcement (summer); KFF or insurer surveys for Medigap
items.cadence: Yearly, in the fall
items.notes: PL_MED_PARTD and HC_PARTD_BASE are the same figure in two places; change both.

items.name: ACA marketplace premiums and subsidies
items.what: Average benchmark Silver premium by state, the poverty line the subsidies are measured against, the subsidy percentages, and whether the enhanced credits are back.
where: web/lib/engine/math.js: HC_FPL_BASE, HC_FPL_PER_ADDL, HC_STATE_PREMIUM_40, the applicable-percentage table below them
web/tools/healthcare/Healthcare.tsx and web/tools/about/About.tsx: the '2026 ACA rules' text
items.source: KFF Marketplace Average Benchmark Premiums (late October or November); HHS poverty guidelines (January, used for the next coverage year); IRS applicable-percentage revenue procedure (summer)
items.cadence: Yearly, for the coming coverage year
items.notes: Coverage year N is priced against the poverty guidelines published in January of N-1, so the 2026 guidelines (already out) are the ones for 2027 coverage.

items.name: RMD and life-expectancy tables
items.what: The IRS Uniform Lifetime Table (RMDs), the Single Life table (72(t) payments), and the RMD starting age, which works out birth year from a hard-coded 2026.
items.source: IRS Publication 590-B
items.cadence: Yearly check. The tables rarely change (last in 2022), but rmdStartAge's year must roll every January
items.notes: rmdStartAge computes birth year as 2026 minus age; leave it and it drifts a year off each January.

items.name: The tax year named in the site's text
items.what: Every place the site says '2026' about its rules: page titles and descriptions, tool badges and headings, the footer, preview cards, articles and FAQs.
items.source: Follows the tax items above
items.cadence: Yearly, on January 1, together with the federal switch
items.notes: Don't change a year that is about history (1926 to 2025) here; the market-history item covers those.

items.name: Stock, bond and inflation history
items.what: Monthly S&P 500 total returns, 10-year Treasury returns, CPI-U inflation and the historical CAPE series, January 1926 onward. Every historical test on the site runs on these.
where: web/lib/engine/math.js: HIST_M_STOCK, HIST_M_BOND, HIST_M_INFL, HIST_M_CAPE (and the '1,200 months' comment)
items.source: Robert Shiller's dataset (Yale), via multpl, for prices, dividends, yields and CAPE; US BLS for CPI-U (December's CPI comes out mid-January)
items.cadence: Yearly: add the past year's 12 months once December's data is in
items.notes: Moves many figures: the articles' worked examples, the homepage and Tools page figures, the numbers baseline, the Guide baseline, the e2e Guide figures, and possibly the preview cards. See UPKEEP.md.

items.name: Cash (T-bill) and small-cap value history
items.what: Monthly one-month Treasury bill and small-company value returns, July 1926 onward.
items.source: Kenneth R. French Data Library (Dartmouth): the Fama-French factors file for T-bills, the 2x3 size/book-to-market portfolios for small value
items.cadence: Yearly, with the market history, once French posts December
items.notes: Must end on the same month as the market history, or the series fall out of step.

items.name: Today's CAPE reading
items.what: The latest Shiller CAPE, shown against the historical record and used by the CAPE withdrawal strategy's 'today' figures.
items.source: multpl.com Shiller PE (monthly)
items.cadence: Monthly
items.notes: check.py reads last_updated and data_for from CAPE_NOW_ASOF, and sets next_due to that date plus max_age_days. Keep the string a plain 'day Month year' date.

items.name: Default mortgage rate
items.what: The 30-year rate the Mortgage and Rent vs. Buy tools start with. The pages call it a starting point, not a live quote.
items.source: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey (weekly); use a rounded recent average
items.cadence: Quarterly, or sooner if rates move more than half a point
items.notes: Changing it moves the Mortgage and Rent vs. Buy figures in the numbers baseline and their articles' worked examples.

items.name: Home price, rent and housing-cost defaults
items.what: The starting home price, rent, rent growth, home appreciation, property tax rate and insurance in the Mortgage and Rent vs. Buy tools.
items.source: NAR or Census median home price; Census or Zillow median rent; Tax Foundation property tax rates
items.cadence: Yearly
items.notes: Round figures on purpose; only change when they're clearly off.

items.name: College cost presets
items.what: The yearly cost of a public in-state and a private school (tuition, room and board) the College Savings tool offers.
where: web/tools/college/model.ts: the presets and default kid
items.source: College Board, Trends in College Pricing (published in late October)
items.cadence: Yearly, after College Board publishes
items.notes: The article quotes $27,000 and a monthly saving figure the tests check.

items.name: 72(t) interest rate default
items.what: The rate the Bridge's 72(t) payment starts with: up to the greater of 5% or 120% of the federal mid-term rate.
items.source: IRS Applicable Federal Rates (monthly revenue rulings)
items.cadence: Quarterly check; only matters if 120% of the mid-term rate goes above 5%

items.name: Debt Payoff example rates
items.what: The example debts' interest rates, mainly the credit card APR.
items.source: Federal Reserve G.19 consumer credit report (credit card rates)
items.cadence: Yearly
items.notes: The tests check the article's worked example against these.

items.name: Long-run assumption defaults
items.what: Default return before inflation (8.5%), inflation (3%), college cost growth (4%), heirs' tax rate and similar starting assumptions.
items.source: Long-run history on the site itself; Vanguard and Morningstar capital-market outlooks as a sanity check
items.cadence: Yearly review; change rarely
items.notes: These are judgment calls, not data. Raise any change with the owner first.

items.name: New laws that change the rules mid-year
items.what: Federal or state legislation that changes brackets, deductions, ACA subsidies (the enhanced credits that expired after 2025), RMD ages or Social Security taxation between the yearly updates.
where: Wherever the law lands; usually web/lib/engine/math.js and the articles
items.source: IRS newsroom, Tax Foundation tracker, KFF for ACA, state revenue departments
items.cadence: Quarterly check

items.name: Article reviews ('Last reviewed' month)
items.what: Each tool page's article shows the month it was last reviewed. A review means checking its figures, sources and links still hold; only then move its date.
items.source: The article's own sources and the site's current figures
items.cadence: Each article every 90 days (set max_age_days to change it)
items.notes: check.py reads every article's data-reviewed date: last_updated is the oldest, next_due is that plus max_age_days. Run node web/scripts/lastmod.mjs after editing an article.
